Natural Selection
¤Directional Selection
  nThe curve shifts in one direction
  nBacteria become resistant to antibiotics
  nIncreasing body size in horse evolution
explanation: Directional selection occurs when natural selection favors one extreme phenotype over others, shifting the phenotypic distribution curve in that direction. The slide provides two classic examples: (1) the evolution of antibiotic resistance in bacteria, where exposure to antibiotics selects for resistant individuals, shifting the population toward resistance; and (2) the evolutionary history of horses, which shows a directional trend toward larger body sizes over millions of years.

questions.q: Which of the following is a real-world example of directional selection described in the notes?
opts: Average human birth weight survival rates
British land snails developing two distinct shell patterns
Moths outside London maintaining constant allele frequencies
questions.exp: Antibiotic resistance in bacteria is a classic example of directional selection, where the selective pressure of antibiotics shifts the population toward the resistant phenotype.
